scoring_notes: Ducommun is a Tier-2/3 sub-contractor; USAspending shows only $19.1M of DIRECT DoD prime awards 2023-2026 (108 contracts), confirming revenue flows through OEM-prime POs (Boeing/RTX/Lockheed/Northrop), not directly. Therefore pentagon_jbook contractor_name='Ducommun' is correctly NOT_FOUND — the test of materiality must be done through the OEM-platform channel implied by cohort metadata (F-35, F/A-18, Apache, Black Hawk). For prime contractor-name queries (Raytheon/Boeing/Lockheed/Northrop), the J-Book corpus only contains ~3-7 PEs per prime out of the prime's full DoD portfolio, so a contractor_name UNFUNDED_THIS_YEAR signal is NOT representative of the prime's overall health — those signals are ignored in favor of program-specific queries.

scores.claim_text: RTX 17.9% of FY2025 net revenues; RTX prime defense programs (Patriot/PAC-3, Tomahawk, SM-6, etc.) underpin Ducommun's #1 customer.
scores.M_value: MIXED: Patriot growing strongly (driven by Ukraine/Pacific demand), Tomahawk collapsing in FY26 procurement
scores.interpretation: RTX itself is healthy at FY26 budget level, but the *mix* shifts: programs Ducommun likely has structural-content on (Patriot launchers, missile cases) accelerate, while Tomahawk content (a legacy Ducommun-relevant launcher/control area) collapses. Net moderate underdelivery risk — the filing offers no breakdown by RTX program so investors cannot calibrate. Materiality is HIGH (18% of revenue), so even moderate program-mix shifts within RTX matter.

scores.claim_text: Boeing 13.3% of FY2025 net revenues — commercial (737 MAX) plus defense (Apache, F/A-18 per cohort metadata).
supports: pentagon_jbook.query_program_funding(program_name='F/A-18') -> NOT_FOUND (consistent with end of Super Hornet procurement)
scores.M_value: Apache procurement -35% FY26; F/A-18 line item absent from J-Book corpus (procurement appears wound down)
scores.interpretation: Material divergence. Boeing-defense exposure for Ducommun runs primarily through Apache (rotor blades, ammunition feed/eject chutes — explicitly disclosed Structural Systems products) and F/A-18 airframe structures. AH-64 Apache Block IIIA Reman is cut 35% in FY26 P-40. F/A-18 procurement has tailed off. Meanwhile Boeing commercial 737 MAX recovery only partially offsets. Filing language: 'Revenue growth with our other commercial customers, including Airbus, and continued solid demand from defense OEMs... have helped to mitigate a significant portion of this risk for the time being' — 'for the time being' is the key hedge. Boeing-defense rotorcraft/fighter exposure is contracting in FY26 J-Book and the filing offers no program-level disclosure that would let investors quantify. Severe because Boeing is the #2 customer and the defense portion has clear J-Book shrinkage.

scores.claim_text: Lockheed Martin 4.2% of FY2025 net revenues (DECLINING from 5.3% FY24); implied F-35 and UH-60 Sikorsky exposure.
scores.M_value: F-35 C2D2 funded steady ~$1.18B FY26; UH-60M Blackhawk MYP procurement TRIPLING in FY26
scores.interpretation: Underlying Lockheed program funding is healthy. The internal contradiction is that Ducommun's *Lockheed customer share* is dropping (5.3%->4.2% YoY) while LMT's F-35 and Black Hawk programs are steady-to-growing in the J-Book. This means Ducommun is LOSING WALLET SHARE inside a growing prime, not riding a shrinking program — which is a competitive-position concern, not a J-Book divergence. Score PASS on the J-Book test (program funding is fine) but flag the wallet-share decline as a separate competitive signal.

scores.claim_text: Northrop 5.8% of FY2025 revenues; AR concentration spiked 2.7%->13.3% YoY suggesting a large single recent shipment.
scores.M_value: B-21 procurement P-40 line shrinking 40% in FY26 after FY25 peak; Sentinel UNVERIFIABLE in corpus
scores.interpretation: The 5x AR concentration spike at Northrop YE2025 (2.7% -> 13.3%) plus B-21 Raider FY26 procurement step-down (-40%) is a coherent pattern of a lumpy ramp-down. The B-21 P-40 procurement going from $2.59B in FY25 to $1.56B in FY26 is a one-year contraction (could be reorganization between LRIP lots), but Ducommun's Northrop exposure likely concentrated in this kind of structural component work. MODERATE because: (a) Northrop is only 5.8% of revenue, (b) B-21 is still a multi-billion program (not zeroed), (c) the AR spike could equally reflect billing timing on a Sentinel ramp-up. Materiality is contained but the AR concentration is a real lumpiness signal.

scores.claim_text: Backlog $1.06B -> $1.20B (+13.4% YoY); growth 'primarily in military and space and commercial aerospace end-use markets' — but no PE-level disclosure of the military backlog composition.
supports: pentagon_jbook.query_program_funding(contractor_name='Ducommun') -> NOT_FOUND (expected — sub-tier supplier not named as primary contractor on any PE)
scores.M_value: Direct DoD prime awards to Ducommun total only $19.1M over 2.5 years — confirms revenue flows via OEM POs, not direct prime awards. J-Book has zero Ducommun-named PEs.
scores.interpretation: The +$142M backlog increase cannot be verified at the program level from public sources because Ducommun is a Tier-2/3 sub. The materiality of this disclosure gap is high: a $1.2B backlog with 'primarily military and space' growth that names zero specific programs is structurally opaque. Without PE-level disclosure, we cannot validate the backlog quality. UNVERIFIABLE per heuristic 7, but the lack of mappability is itself the meta-finding scored under C10.

scores.claim_text: Structural Systems supplies rotor blades on rotor-wing aircraft and ammunition feed/eject chutes for fixed- and rotary-wing military aircraft and military ground vehicles.
supports: pentagon_jbook.query_program_funding(program_name='F-15') -> UNFUNDED_TWO_PLUS_YEARS (F-15 EPAWSS, but EPAWSS is electronics-mod not airframe — not directly Ducommun-relevant)
pentagon_jbook.query_program_funding(program_name='F-16') -> FUNDED_GROWING (Foreign Military Sales driven; $120M FY24 -> $217M FY26)
scores.M_value: Apache rotor blade / ammo chute volume contracting; UH-60M and F-16 production growing; F/A-18 production likely ended (NOT_FOUND in corpus); F-15 EPAWSS unfunded but not airframe-relevant
scores.interpretation: MIXED picture for the named structural product lines. Apache rotorcraft work shrinks 35% in FY26. UH-60M Blackhawk MYP (Sikorsky/Lockheed) triples — strongly positive for Ducommun if they have content on the M-model. F-16 FMS growing. The Apache contraction is material because Apache rotor blades + ammo handling are explicitly disclosed Ducommun product lines. Net: MODERATE underdelivery — Apache headwind exceeds UH-60 tailwind in dollar terms ($195M Apache cut vs $513M UH-60 increase, but Ducommun's share of each is unknown and Apache is a more mature/higher-content program for them historically).

scores.claim_text: FY2026 capex $20-24M 'principally to support new contract awards in Electronic Systems and Structural Systems'; tooling for 'newer programs which have higher engineering content.'
scores.M_value: Direct DoD obligations to Ducommun running ~$9-10M/year — too small to validate a $20-24M tooling capex against named programs
scores.interpretation: Forward capex statement is unverifiable at the program level: the company names no specific 'new contract awards' driving the tooling. The capex amount ($20-24M) is comparable to ALL of Ducommun's direct DoD obligations over 16 months ($12M), suggesting the new awards are sub-contracts via OEMs (not direct primes). Cannot validate against J-Book without OEM-level identification. UNVERIFIABLE.

scores.claim_text: Boeing 737 MAX FAA-cleared production rate increase from 38/mo to 42/mo — Ducommun states this 'mitigates a significant portion' of Boeing-quality risk.
supports: Ducommun cites Boeing's own 10-K + public FAA statements; this is a control claim (non-J-Book commercial aerospace)
scores.M_value: Statement is consistent with Boeing's own disclosed FY2025 narrative and publicly announced production rate trajectory.
scores.interpretation: Control claim. Commercial aerospace, not J-Book-related. The 737 MAX rate-up to 42/mo is publicly known and Boeing has disclosed it. PASS. (Note: the company's own framing 'for the time being' is appropriately hedged.)

scores.claim_text: April 2023 BLR Aerospace acquisition — aerodynamic systems for rotary and fixed-wing aircraft, commercial and military platforms, added to Structural Systems.
supports: Control claim — rollup thesis; BLR is small aerodynamic-systems specialist; integration is now ~3 years old
scores.M_value: N/A — no incoherent-acquisition pattern evident; BLR is an in-vertical, capability-additive deal
scores.interpretation: Control claim. BLR is coherent with Ducommun's Structural Systems portfolio (rotary/fixed-wing aerodynamic systems, near-aftermarket). No 'desperation pivot' signal. PASS.

scores.claim_text: META-claim: DCO 10-K names ZERO specific Pentagon Program Elements and ZERO specific named DoD programs (no F-35, F-18, Apache, Black Hawk, B-21, Patriot, Tomahawk, etc.) despite ~28% prime-defense revenue exposure and 96% A&D mix.
supports: Exhaustive keyword search of the 88,877-char sliced 10-K confirms zero hits on any named Pentagon program designator

usaspending.query_dod_contracts(recipient_name='Ducommun') -> only $19.1M direct DoD obligations vs ~$400M+ implied defense revenue — confirms revenue flows through OEM POs that the company does not specify
scores.M_value: DISCLOSURE OPACITY: ~28% of revenue ($210M+ at 18% RTX + 6% Northrop + 4% Lockheed of ~$830M revenue base) flows through DoD-prime channels with zero PE-level identification. Investors cannot map the $1.2B backlog to specific J-Book lines.
scores.interpretation: This is the J-Book divergence pattern inverted: rather than over-claiming on a named PE that's unfunded (IONQ/YSS canonical), Ducommun under-claims by naming zero PEs at all. The risk is asymmetric because the J-Book reveals MIXED conditions in the implied Ducommun-relevant programs: Apache -35% FY26, B-21 -40% FY26, F/A-18 production wound down, F-15 EPAWSS unfunded 2+ years — offset by UH-60 +185%, F-16 +81%, F-35 steady, Patriot +340%. A sub-tier supplier with disclosed material customer concentration (RTX 18%, Boeing 13%, Northrop 6%, Lockheed 4%, Viasat 4%) and a growing $1.2B backlog has a duty to identify the underlying program mix; the absence of any such disclosure leaves investors unable to assess whether the growing backlog is exposed to the FY26 Apache/B-21/F/A-18 contractions or the UH-60/F-16/F-35/Patriot expansions. Coupled with the Northrop AR concentration spike (2.7% -> 13.3%, a 5x jump) right as B-21 procurement steps down 40%, the opacity is materially load-bearing. RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE on disclosure quality, not on a specific named-PE divergence.

summary.headline_finding: DCO is a Tier-2/3 aerospace structures + electronics sub-contractor. The 10-K discloses ONLY customer-level concentration and end-use markets, NO specific Pentagon Program Elements or named DoD programs. Through the implied OEM channel, J-Book reveals MIXED FY26 conditions: Apache -35%, B-21 -40%, F/A-18 wound-down, F-15 EPAWSS unfunded, all offset by UH-60 +185%, F-16 +81%, F-35 steady, Patriot +340%. The headline issue is DISCLOSURE OPACITY — investors cannot map the growing $1.2B backlog to specific J-Book exposures, which combined with a 5x YoY Northrop AR concentration spike (2.7% -> 13.3%) right as B-21 procurement contracts is the material red flag.
